itinerary.cal: A June-to-July objective while the Mowich face still holds snow and ice; both opened 2012 reports found the headwall icefall out of shape by August. Requires a Mount Rainier climbing permit and wilderness camp permit, and as a Mowich-to-White River traverse it usually takes 3-4 days with a car shuttle.
itinerary.totalNote: A 3-4 day traverse: up from Mowich Lake to a Ptarmigan Ridge camp, across the North Mowich Glacier to a high camp below the headwall, over Liberty Cap, and down the Emmons to Camp Schurman and White River.

days.title: Mowich Lake to Ptarmigan Ridge camp
days.objective: Reach the lower Ptarmigan Ridge bivy
days.note: Take the trail to Spray Park and follow the ridge toward Observation Rock. The 2012 parties camped at about 8,200 ft and 8,600 ft on Ptarmigan Ridge above the North Mowich Glacier.

days.title: Cross the North Mowich to high camp
days.objective: Move camp to about 10,000 ft below the headwall
days.note: Drop off the ridge on the snow fingers near 8,200 ft rather than lower down the scree; one party found descending to 8,500 ft on scree a mistake. Bivy sites around 9,200 ft are scarce, and one party camped just below the headwall near 10,000 ft, wearing helmets because of icefall.

days.title: Climb the headwall over Liberty Cap
days.objective: Top out on Liberty Cap and start down the Emmons
days.note: Leave before dawn. If the hourglass icefall is out of shape, the 2012 party used a snow ramp onto the central Mowich face instead, finishing on steep, sustained snow under a rock band. They needed an unplanned bivy between Liberty Cap and the summit, so carry bivy gear over the top.

days.title: Descend the Emmons to White River
days.objective: Return via Camp Schurman to the White River trailhead
days.note: Descend the Emmons-Winthrop route past Camp Schurman and out the Glacier Basin trail. One 2012 party descended Disappointment Cleaver to Paradise instead.

prior.notes: Neither opened source climbs the North Mowich Headwall itself. Upwardescape (Aug 2012) found the headwall icefall out of shape, used a snow ramp onto the central face, camped at 8,600 ft and about 10,000 ft, bivied near Liberty Cap and descended the DC, not the Emmons. Turns-all-year (Jul 2012) camped at 8,200 ft on the North Mowich and climbed the central face. Day gains come from the row's 4,955 ft trailhead and 14,112 ft high point plus the source camp elevations. Row dist_km 27.36 (17.0 mi) fits a one-way Mowich-to-White River traverse; no source splits it by day, so day miles are left blank. The search found only a SummitPost Mowich Headwall page (403).

itinerary.cal: A late-summer scramble once the Heineken gullies and the ridge are snow-free; earlier in the season expect steep snow that calls for an axe and crampons. Usually done as one long loop, with a bike stashed for the road back.
itinerary.totalNote: A single long day: about 20 miles and 8,700 ft of gain from Bedal Creek over Heineken Peak, up the NE ridge, and down through Glacier Basin and Monte Cristo, in just over 12 hours.

days.title: Bedal Creek over Heineken to Cadet
days.objective: Climb the NE ridge and loop out through Glacier Basin
days.note: Follow the brushy Bedal Creek trail into the basin under Sloan, climb about 1,000 ft to the ridge, and refill at Cadet Lake. The crux is the descent off Heineken, down steep, wet grass gullies to a 5,600 ft low point above the Mayflower Glacier. The NE ridge itself is class 3 at most on solid rock, with a scramble bypass and meltwater at the hanging glacier. Descend the steep, loose slope into Glacier Basin, walk out past Monte Cristo, and bike down from Barlow Pass.

prior.notes: Only climberkyle (Sept 2023) describes this route: 20 mi including about 6 mi of downhill biking, 8,700 ft, just over 12 h car to car. WTA's Cadet Peak page covers only the Glacier Basin exit (16 mi RT, 5,000 ft, 7,186 ft summit, class 3), so this rests on one route source. A SummitPost snippet suggests a two-day version camping at Cadet Lake, but that page returns 403.

itinerary.cal: A summer scramble from mid-July into September once the north-side snow has gone; the Enchantment permit area limits overnight use, so parties do it as one long day. An Alpine Lakes Wilderness self-issue day permit is required.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: roughly 5,200 ft from the Stuart Lake trailhead, mostly cross-country through forest, brush and talus to the 8,638 ft summit.

days.title: Stuart Lake trail to Cannon summit
days.objective: Scramble the NW ridge to the summit and return
days.note: Leave the Stuart Lake trail before the Mountaineer Creek bridge (sources give 0.5-1.3 mi) and climb south through forest and brush to a flat area near 5,000 ft before heading up toward the ridge. The summit block is a steep friction slab. Early in the season the north slopes hold steep snow.

prior.notes: Neither opened source climbs the NW ridge proper. Both use this approach as a one-day trip: hippohamster climbed the SW ridge (8.62 mi, 5,200 ft, about 13 h, summit about 6 h after a 5:30 am start), and Wenatchee Outdoors skied the NW face (summit ridge by 1:30 pm). Gain comes from the row's 3,404 ft trailhead to its 8,638 ft summit waypoint. Hours and miles are left blank because the only figures are for other lines. Search snippets of a 2016 Mountaineers report and a 2013 CascadeClimbers TR call the NW ridge a long, non-technical scramble, but both pages return 403. NOTE: the row's high_point_ft is null while its summit waypoint is labeled 'NE Ridge route point'.

itinerary.cal: Best from mid-July to early October when the high basin is reachable; water in the basin tarns becomes unreliable after mid-August. Glacier Peak Wilderness self-issue permit; most parties take 3 days and add Saska and Emerald from the same camp.
itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day trip: walk up the North Fork Entiat to a high meadow camp near 6,800 ft, climb Cardinal (often with Saska and Emerald) on day 2, and walk out on day 3.

days.title: North Fork Entiat to the high basin
days.objective: Camp in the basin between Emerald and Saska
days.note: About 8 miles of trail to Fox Camp, the last certain water, then about 1.5 miles more on the Pyramid trail to the basin. Climberkyle's party camped in a meadow near 6,800 ft below Cardinal after a long day with heavy packs.

days.title: Climb Cardinal from the northwest basin
days.objective: Reach the 8,590 ft summit and return to camp
days.note: Climb the snow in Cardinal's northwest basin to the summit ridge, then scramble the exposed ridge to the top, with some slab moves in boots. Parties linking Saska and Emerald first did not reach Cardinal until evening, so climb it first if it is the priority.

days.title: Walk out the North Fork Entiat
days.note: Reverse the approach; climberkyle's party found the walk out somewhat faster.

prior.notes: Neither source names the NW couloir or north ridge. Lemke climbed snow in Cardinal's NW basin to the summit ridge and then the exposed ridge (8,590 ft summit), approaching from Lake Chelan. Climberkyle took the Entiat side in 3 days with a 6,800 ft meadow camp, but did not name the Cardinal line. Day 1/3 miles (8 + 1.5) and the 3,880 ft trailhead come from the row's bivy notes. Day 2 gain runs from the 6,800 ft camp to the 8,590 ft summit, ignoring any intermediate dips.

itinerary.cal: Snow-free from about mid-July through September; earlier, steep snow on the north side calls for an axe and sometimes crampons. Overnight use needs an Enchantment permit, so most parties go car to car in one long day.
itinerary.totalNote: One long day of about 17 miles and 5,200-5,700 ft via Eightmile Lake, Lake Caroline and Windy Pass, finishing on class 3 north-side rock.

days.title: Eightmile trailhead to Cashmere summit
days.objective: Traverse the north side to the summit and return
days.note: Take the Eightmile Lake trail, turn off past Little Eightmile Lake toward Lake Caroline, and continue about 2 miles past the lake to Windy Pass. Follow the ridge northeast past the west-peak spires, cross to the north side, and traverse low below the summit pyramid to a class 3 gully or saddle that leads to the tiny summit. Wear helmets and keep the party close in the gullies.

prior.notes: Both sources describe the standard north-side finish from Windy Pass (Outbound: traverse to a saddle just west of the summit, then a gully south; Wenatchee Outdoors: a class 3 gully that avoids 4th class), but neither calls it the northeast ridge, so the last few hundred feet may differ from the row's route. Figures: Outbound 17 mi RT / 5,700 ft; Wenatchee Outdoors 8.5-9 mi one way / 5,200-5,300 ft. Neither gives a time, so hours are blank.

itinerary.cal: July through September; the east-facing slopes below the wall get sun most of the day and can slide while snow remains. No permit is needed, and parties climb it in a single day from the highway, sometimes from a bivy in the south basin.
itinerary.totalNote: One day: about 2 miles from the highway into the basin east of the peak, six pitches (two of them 5.10) on the East Face, then down the South Buttress or West Ridge.

days.title: Climb the East Face of Cutthroat
days.objective: Climb the face to the false summit and descend
days.note: From the pullout west of Washington Pass, take the cairned track down to cross State Creek and up into the basin south of the peak (about two hours with a pack). Round the base of the South Buttress into the east basin rather than taking the loose scree chimneys below the wall. Descend by the South Buttress (single 60 m rope) or the West Ridge if the buttress is busy.

prior.notes: No opened source describes this 1976 Bard/Chouinard/Cunningham line pitch by pitch; the AAJ Swarm report only mentions it as 'farther right on the face'. A SummitPost snippet (page 403) gives III 5.10, 6 pitches, ending on the false summit. The approach and descent come from the AAJ (about 2 mi from the highway into the east basin) and Mountain Project (South Buttress and Swarm pages). Miles assume 2 mi each way. Gain runs from the row's 5,227 ft pullout to its 8,066 ft summit, and the two-hour basin figure is from the row's bivy notes. CONTRADICTION: the row's dist_km of 2 (1.2 mi) is shorter than AAJ's about 2 mi, and its gain_ft of 2,500 is below 5,227 to 8,066 ft.

itinerary.cal: A late-summer objective once the upper snow patch on the face has melted; it needs a North Cascades National Park wilderness permit for the Eldorado-area cross-country camps. Plan about 4 days, or 3 with a camp at Dorado Col or on the Marble Creek bench.
itinerary.totalNote: About 4 days: the Eldorado approach to a lower and then a high camp near the East Ridge, a long climb day over Dorado Col to the 8-pitch Southwest Face, and a walk out.

days.title: Eldorado trailhead to lower camp
days.objective: Reach the lower camp near 5,400 ft
days.note: The standard Eldorado climbers' route is steep and is the hardest day of the trip with an overnight pack.

days.title: Up to the East Ridge high camp
days.objective: Camp near 7,800 ft at the base of Eldorado's East Ridge
days.note: Climb along the southern edge of the Inspiration Glacier to the bivy at the base of the East Ridge. Dorado Col and a bench near 6,000 ft in the Marble Creek cirque are alternative camps closer to the climb.

days.title: Climb the Southwest Face
days.objective: Cross Dorado Col, climb 8 pitches and return to camp
days.note: Cross the Inspiration and McAllister glaciers to Dorado Col, descend bare ice and snow to about 6,000 ft, and contour west on a bench to a snow gully below the face. The route follows the main crack system (wet 5.9 roof crux) to the ridge crest, then several low-fifth pitches on poorer rock. The NPS party descended by a single-rope rappel west to the Marble Creek glacier, then a loose gully rappel and a moat, and retraced their route over Dorado Col.

days.title: Walk out to the Eldorado trailhead
days.objective: Descend from high camp to the car
days.note: Reverse the Eldorado approach from about 7,800 ft to the trailhead near 2,100 ft.

prior.notes: NPS and Mountain Project both describe this route (8 pitches, 1,400 ft, 5.9, approach over Dorado Col and the Marble Creek cirque) and the NPS camps, but no opened source gives a time for any day. Day 1-2 gains and camp elevations (2,100 / 5,400 / 7,800 ft) come from North Cascades Mountain Guides' Eldorado itinerary. Day 3 gain counts only the 1,400 ft route; the re-climb from the 6,000 ft bench back over Dorado Col is not given by any source and is not counted. The row has no gain or distance to compare.

itinerary.cal: A short day climb best in early summer while some snow lingers below the gully, or later once it is dry; the gully itself can run with water. Park at the Esmeralda/Ingalls trailhead with a recreation pass and self-issue a free Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit.
itinerary.totalNote: One day, about 5 miles round trip and roughly 2,300 ft of gain: up the East Peak's east gully and down south to the De Roux Creek trail.

days.title: Climb the East Gully and loop out
days.objective: Climb the east gully to the 6,480 ft East Peak and descend to De Roux
days.note: Cross the North Fork Teanaway on a small log jam near the trailhead, bushwhack and climb talus or snow to the gully, and expect loose Class 3-4 with a wet, poorly protected section about 500 ft up that the reference party escaped by a short chimney and low 5th-class rock on the right. Rejoin the gully at a small horn and follow the ridge left to the top. Descend 400-500 ft south, traverse down to the ridge north of the De Roux Creek trail, and walk the trail and an old road about 2 miles back to the trailhead.

prior.notes: Only one opened source (ericsbasecamp) describes this route: East Gully of the 6,480 ft east summit from the Ingalls Lake trailhead, about 5 mi round trip, roped up for Class 4 and low 5th; the USFS page only confirms the 4,269 ft trailhead and permits. Gain equals row gain_ft 2,280, consistent with ericsbasecamp's ~4,200 ft start and 6,480 ft summit. Row dist_km 8.05 (5.0 mi) matches the round trip, not one way. No hours given. The source rates parts of the line low 5th class, harder than the row's Class 4.

itinerary.cal: A June to early-July snow line, before crevasses on the White Salmon open up and the lower Avalanche Glacier goes mushy. A Cascade Volcano Pass is required above 7,000 ft from April through October; documented parties did it car-to-car in a day from Cold Springs, with a camp in the 7,200 ft moraine bowl as the option for a shorter summit day.
itinerary.totalNote: Usually one long day from Cold Springs; parties wanting a camp can use the moraine bowl at about 7,200 ft where the Avalanche Glacier begins.

days.title: Cold Springs to the summit and back
days.objective: Climb the Avalanche and White Salmon glaciers to the summit
days.note: Take the South Climb trail to the Round the Mountain Trail and traverse about 2 miles northwest to the Avalanche Glacier outlet stream near 6,100 ft, then follow moraines to the bowl at 7,200 ft. The Avalanche Glacier was uncrevassed in 2004, while the White Salmon has seracs on its north and west sides and a short 45-degree pitch to the saddle between the summit and the Pinnacle; a moraine saddle at about 10,200 ft links the two glaciers.

schedule.label: Leave Cold Springs
schedule.detail: 2004 party's start (they climbed the South Spur and descended this line).

schedule.label: Round the Mountain Trail
schedule.detail: Back at 6,100 ft after descending the White Salmon and Avalanche glaciers.

prior.notes: All three opened sources are ski trips: the 2004 and 2012 parties climbed another way from Cold Springs and skied this line in a day (times above are the 2004 party's, so an ascent of the glaciers will differ), and the 2014 party camped at about 6,800 ft from Williams Mine and turned back at 9,200 ft. Gain is derived from the row's Cold Springs elevation (5,600 ft) and Adams' 12,276 ft summit; row gain, distance and high point are null. No source gives mileage.
